system_description.narrative_title: Iran war: stalemate, economic warfare and global market spillovers
system_description.narrative_summary: Six months into the Iran war the dominant story is a costly military stalemate that has been met with a parallel campaign of economic warfare — sanctions, banking restrictions and efforts to choke oil exports — rather than decisive battlefield outcomes. That campaign is reshaping global energy and financial flows as the US, regional Gulf states, China and Russia jockey for influence, producing market volatility, alternative trade channels, infrastructure investment shifts, and rising political and logistical feedbacks across regions. The dynamic is open-ended: sanctions and blockades depress Iran's revenue and prompt circumvention (through Dubai, Chinese buyers, or new pipelines), which in turn drives more coercive measures and regional tensions, while commodity shocks feed domestic political pressure and policy responses in importing countries.
system_description.scope: Inside the system boundary: the Iran war (military actions and stalemate), US-led sanctions and Treasury actions against banks and branches, measures to choke Iranian oil (blockades, export interdiction), responses by China/Russia/Gulf states (trade, financing, diplomatic pushback), impacts on global energy markets and shipping, regional security incidents (Israel, Syria, Turkey), and secondary economic effects (fuel surcharges, refinery/auto sales impacts, munitions drain, infrastructure investment).
system_description.super_system: Global geopolitical-economy (international security, energy markets, and cross-border finance)
adjacent_subsystems: Global energy markets (oil, LNG, shipping, OPEC+ dynamics)
International financial system and sanctions architecture (bank clearing, dollar flows, crypto alternatives)
Middle East regional security dynamics (state and militia interactions, Israel/Arab states/Turkey)
Global supply chains and commodity markets (manufacturing, automotive, refined fuels)

variables.name: Military conflict intensity
variables.description: Measures the scale, frequency, and lethality of kinetic military operations in the conflict zone.

variables.name: Military stalemate degree
variables.description: Measures the persistence of frozen frontlines and lack of decisive battlefield shifts.

variables.name: Economic warfare intensity
variables.description: Measures the scope and severity of economic coercion including sanctions, blockades, and financial restrictions.

variables.name: Sanctions enforcement strength
variables.description: Measures the rigor, coverage, and operational effectiveness of sanctioning and interdiction activities.

variables.name: Oil export constraint
variables.description: Measures the degree to which oil export flows are physically or administratively constrained or interdicted.

variables.name: Oil price volatility
variables.description: Measures the amplitude and frequency of price swings in global oil markets.

variables.name: Shipping disruption risk
variables.description: Measures the probability and severity of disruptions to maritime shipping and logistics routes.

variables.name: Alternative trade channel use
variables.description: Measures the prevalence and volume of trade rerouted through nonstandard intermediaries, informal hubs, or alternate routes.

variables.name: Banking access restriction
variables.description: Measures limitations on correspondent banking, clearing access, and participation in international payment systems.

variables.name: Financial transaction freeze rate
variables.description: Measures the frequency and scale of account freezes, payment blocks, and transaction denials affecting cross-border flows.

variables.name: Regional security incident rate
variables.description: Measures the rate of security incidents, cross-border clashes, and targeted attacks within the wider region.

variables.name: Munitions consumption rate
variables.description: Measures the rate at which military munitions, ammunition, and expendables are expended in operations.

variables.name: Domestic political pressure
variables.description: Measures domestic economic and political stress, including protests, panic buying, and unrest driven by commodity shocks and sanctions.

variables.name: Energy infrastructure investment shift
variables.description: Measures the rate and direction of investment reallocations toward pipelines, ports, refineries, and related energy infrastructure.

variables.name: Global fuel supply tightness
variables.description: Measures spare capacity, inventories, and shortfalls across global fuel and refined products markets.

variables.name: Cross-border finance rerouting
variables.description: Measures the extent to which cross-border financial flows are redirected through alternative channels, currencies, or intermediaries.

catalysts.title: U.S. campaign targets Dubai banking ties
catalysts.description: Continued U.S. pressure and sanctions actions aimed at Dubai and UAE-linked banks, expanding enforcement against regional clearing and correspondent services.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'US campaign to isolate Iran closes in on Dubai', 'Treasury moves to sanction UAE branch of Egyptian bank'.

catalysts.title: Russia extends diesel export ban to Sept 30
catalysts.description: Moscow's formal extension of diesel export restrictions through September 30 will tighten refined-fuel markets and reshape trade flows.
catalysts.rationale: Headline: 'Russia extends ban on diesel exports until September 30' (2026-08-29).

catalysts.title: U.S. naval interdiction of Iran oil exports
catalysts.description: Ongoing U.S. maritime interdiction and blockade measures further slash Iran's seaborne oil exports, sustaining supply constraints and market reactions.
catalysts.rationale: Headline: 'U.S. Navy blockade slashes Iran oil exports as Trump administration shifts to economic warfare'.

catalysts.title: Conflict reaches persistent stalemate
catalysts.description: The war continues in a Ukraine-style, costly stalemate with frozen frontlines and recurring low-level kinetic activity, prolonging economic and social effects.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'Six months into the Iran war: Markets become accustomed to stalemate', 'approaching Ukraine-style stalemate'.

catalysts.title: U.S.-hosted G20 finance meeting targets Iran sanctions
catalysts.description: A planned G20 finance meeting will discuss sanctions, growth and imbalances, potentially coordinating tighter financial measures against Iran and allies.
catalysts.rationale: Headline: 'US-hosted G20 finance meeting to target growth, imbalances, Iran sanctions'.

catalysts.title: China may shield markets and retaliate over sanctions
catalysts.description: Chinese warnings and large oil reserves create scope for Beijing to blunt sanctions effects, provide support to markets, and retaliate diplomatically or economically.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'China warns US it could retaliate over Iran sanctions', 'China’s massive oil reserves give Beijing leverage'.

catalysts.title: U.S. munitions drain and procurement pressure
catalysts.description: Heavy use of munitions in the conflict is straining U.S. stocks and prompting accelerated procurement and political concern about readiness.
catalysts.rationale: Headline: 'Drain on U.S. Munitions From Iran War Raises Fears Over Ability to Deter China, Russia'.

catalysts.title: UAE probes Banque Misr; dollar clearing limited
catalysts.description: Investigations and U.S. limits on Egyptian banks' UAE branches may curtail dollar clearing, prompting account freezes and re-routing of finance.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'UAE investigates Egypt’s Banque Misr', 'US hits Egyptian bank branches with Iran sanctions'.

catalysts.title: Risk of wider regional incidents increases
catalysts.description: Cross-border strikes, West Bank incidents and probing strikes near Turkey raise the chance of spillover clashes across the region.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'Israel’s Syria strike may have been bid to provoke Turkey conflict', 'Israeli settlers stage new attack', 'Israel kills Hamas operative'.
